problem: Model-based RL agents such as DreamerV3 are limited by the accuracy of their amortised world-model encoder in unfamiliar settings, and fixing this normally requires more training or added planning modules.
motivation: System-2-like deliberate reasoning could help agents cope with unfamiliar situations without large amounts of extra data. The authors observe that the learned world model already contains amortised experience. Backpropagating through its imagined future rollouts can therefore refine the current state without new parameters.
key_idea: At decision time, take gradient steps on the agent's current latent state (recurrent state h_t) to minimise an uncertainty-based objective (state or parameter information gain) computed over imagined latent rollouts, so that the state is coherent with the world model's predicted future; no training is needed.
insight: State-IG with a short rollout (lambda=1) mainly closes the amortisation gap of the current-state reconstruction. Longer rollouts (lambda=8/16) barely change the current reconstruction but shift the agent's trajectory toward states that are reconstructed more accurately, and this is clearest in partially-observable 3D tasks (Fig. natlab_trajectories). On Miniworld the gains concentrate on episodes where the baseline does worst: baseline -0.11 vs SIG 0.61 for episodes with baseline score below 0.25, while the overall average is unchanged. Entropy as an objective gave no significant gains, which supports focusing on model-evidence-derived objectives.
method: Base agent: a pre-trained DreamerV3 (large) world model and actor, kept frozen; iterative inference (II) is applied after every environment step.
Latent imagination rollouts: from the current state, roll the sequence model, dynamics prior and actor forward lambda in {1,3,8,16} steps, averaging over s=3 sampled trajectories per gradient step.
State update: n=10 gradient steps on h_t with step size alpha, backpropagating through the rollouts and the actor. z_t and the actions are taken as modes (deterministic) for both II and the baseline.
State Information Gain (SIG) objective: KL between the posterior computed from decoder-reconstructed imagined observations and the dynamics prior, averaged over the rollout.
Parameter Information Gain (PIG) objective: latent disagreement, i.e. the variance of a Plan2Explore ensemble's predictions of z, averaged over the rollout.
Entropy (ENT) objective: entropy of the prior over imagined latents, used as a comparison objective.
Regulariser: a KL between the initial and updated posterior with free bits (max(1, KL)), scaled to the objective's magnitude, so the updated state stays faithful to the current observation.

setting.backbone: DreamerV3 large (pre-trained per task, frozen at test time, with the Plan2Explore latent-disagreement ensemble)
setting.training_data: none for II itself (training-free); the DreamerV3 base agents are pre-trained on each task's environment interaction (100K-30M steps)
setting.observation: monocular first-person RGB images (DMLab, Miniworld) and Atari frames
setting.simulator: DeepMind Lab (Collect Good Objects, NatLab Fixed Large Map), Atari Alien, custom Miniworld Y-maze

numbers.eval_set_note: all matched-initialisation episodes (1M pre-training steps); each row is an increasingly restricted subset of episodes where the baseline score is below a threshold; 'All' = 100% of episodes
numbers.method: DreamerV3 + Iterative Inference, State IG (best lambda)
numbers.extra: Score is reward in the custom task; Baseline score in the same episodes is 0.68 (All), 0.55 (<0.90), 0.44 (<0.75), 0.19 (<0.50), -0.11 (<0.25), -0.20 (<0.00); best lambda varies per row (16 for All, 1 for the rest)
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Miniworld task performance after 1M pre-training steps), SIG column

numbers.eval_set_note: same threshold-selected episodes as the SIG row
numbers.method: DreamerV3 + Iterative Inference, Parameter IG (best lambda)
numbers.extra: best lambda 3 for most rows and 8 for the two lowest thresholds

numbers_note: Main results for DMLab and Atari (reconstruction metrics PSNR/SSIM/MSE and task score vs pre-training volume) are given only in figures, so no numbers are extracted. Miniworld is a custom task, not a standard navigation benchmark.
results: II with State IG or Parameter IG gives consistent improvements over the default DreamerV3 in reconstruction metrics (PSNR/SSIM) on both DMLab tasks and Atari, with the largest gains on the complex partially-observable DMLab 2. Task performance improves mainly for agents with less pre-training and for episodes where the baseline does poorly, e.g. Miniworld score -0.11 -> 0.61 for baseline scores below 0.25. Longer rollouts help partially-observable tasks but not fully-observable Atari, and enough further training of the baseline can beat II.
limitations: Applied at every step with n=10 gradient steps over multiple rollouts, so it is computationally expensive, and there is no mechanism to detect when the agent is 'in doubt' or to halt early.

Evaluated only on DreamerV3 and a few small visual tasks (results in figures, mostly with statistical significance testing over 100 episodes), and it depends on a good world model; step size and rollout length need per-volume tuning.
Task-performance gains are inconsistent: reconstruction gains do not always translate into better scores, II can hurt in episodes where the baseline does well, and gains vanish with enough training.
